clue.text: Flood's ending with Noah's vessel in gloom

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of Flood's is used

parts.note: Noah built the ark to survive the Flood

explanation.surface: After the Flood subsides, Noah's boat sits in the gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness and gloom are both an absence of light, so the noun fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Remoteness of girl with attitude

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
a stance is a position or attitude on an issue

explanation.surface: A girl with a bad attitude seems cold and remote.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance in the sense of aloofness or the state of being far away, a synonym.

clue.text: Tough character reflected partially in Jacob Marley

indicators.note: reflected says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hard man is seen mirrored in Marley's ghost from A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambo is the hard-bitten action hero of the Sylvester Stallone films, a byword for toughness.

clue.text: Come down with post for remote Cornish location

parts.note: a plane comes down when it lands
to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: A traveller lands and mails something from the far tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, in the county of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The headland is the far south-western tip of Britain, a famously distant spot.

clue.text: Tune I like, yodelled at first in casual manner

parts.note: an air is a melody or tune

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of like and yodelled

explanation.surface: A singer says they enjoy a tune that was yodelled, sounding offhand.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something airily means lightly and nonchalantly, without concern.

clue.text: Very resistant to once more entering lifeless street

indicators.note: entering puts the word for once more inside the other two pieces

parts.note: dead means lifeless
again means once more

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to go back into a deserted street.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead against something is the idiom for being wholly opposed to it.

clue.text: Lug part of bale, or last of produce, carelessly

indicators.note: carelessly means done sloppily, so these letters end up rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of produce

explanation.surface: A farm hand carelessly handles a bale or the last of the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: Lug is an informal British word for ear, so 'Lug part' is the definition rather than a verb about hauling bales.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fleshy piece hanging at the bottom of the ear is part of a lug.

clue.text: Toy handed to grateful girl, last of all

indicators.note: last of all takes the final letter of every one of the four words that follow Toy

explanation.surface: A plaything is given to a thankful girl at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: A doll is a child's plaything in human form, an example of a toy.

clue.text: Remains after rearranging student meeting

indicators.note: the letters of Remains are put in a new order to give the answer

explanation.surface: Something is left over once a student gathering has been reorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: A university class where a small group of students discuss a topic with a tutor.

clue.text: As uitlander, potentially, awarded citizenship?

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreigner might be granted citizenship.
explanation.walkthrough: Uitlander is Afrikaans for foreigner, an outsider in South Africa, which is what makes the surface so fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturalised person has been granted citizenship of a country they were not born in.

clue.text: Annual percentage rate, one lowered initially for a month

parts.note: APR is the standard abbreviation for annual percentage rate on loans
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of lowered

explanation.surface: A lender's interest rate is cut at the start of a particular month.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth calendar month, one example of the twelve months of the year.

clue.text: Drunk a lot on a mild sherry

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and muddled, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has drunk a great deal of a gentle sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as describing what the drinker did, but it is the signal that the following words are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a type of Spanish sherry, medium-dry and darker than fino: an example of the category.

clue.text: One pursuing, perhaps, article in Spanish for comic verse

parts.note: one who dogs someone follows them closely, so a dogger is a pursuer
el is the Spanish masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A chaser, or maybe a Spanish article, could produce some silly verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is badly made, often comic, rhyming poetry.

clue.text: Cold German gentleman with yen for fruit

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Herr is the German for Mr or gentleman
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A chilly German man swaps his money for some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round stone fruit, red or black, is one example of a fruit.

clue.text: One in recession, ie bachelor, ruined with debt

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An economic slump leaves a single man ruined and in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recession' suggests the economy, but here it means the water receding.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb tide is the falling tide, the time when the sea draws back.

clue.text: Awoke close to eight, in brief dramatic appearance

indicators.note: in puts the final letter of eight inside the word for the short appearance

parts.note: a cameo is a brief appearance by a well-known actor

indicators.note: close to means the end, so the final letter of eight is taken

explanation.surface: An actor makes a short stage appearance at nearly eight o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, so the past tense matches having woken up.

clue.text: Clever bishop — rather wet?

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
rainy weather is fairly wet

explanation.surface: A clever bishop is mocked as a bit of a wet, feeble type.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainy is an informal adjective for intelligent.

clue.text: Attractive girl we hear going round for job in church?

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the girl is used only for how it is spoken

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful girl or woman
ringing something is encircling it, going round it

explanation.surface: We learn that a pretty girl is circling, perhaps in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLE and BELL are pronounced the same, so the first piece is spelt as the church bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounding the bells is a task done in churches, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Pinot Noir, as regularly found in ancient part of Asia

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting from the second, of the phrase

explanation.surface: Red wine is found in an ancient region of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionia was the Greek-settled coastal region of western Asia Minor in antiquity.

clue.text: Capital city's outskirts evacuated, behold

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of outskirts

parts.note: lo is an old word for behold

explanation.surface: A city's suburbs have been emptied: look!
explanation.walkthrough: 'city's' belongs to the definition, with the 's standing for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

clue.text: Sends up European surrounded by runners

indicators.note: surrounded by says the European letter sits within the runners

parts.note: skis run along snow, and are the runners of a sledge-like kind

explanation.surface: Someone launches a European skier upward between racers.
explanation.walkthrough: To sky a ball is to hit it high into the air, so 'Sends up' is a verb, not satire.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and other ball games, to sky the ball is to hit it steeply upward.

clue.text: One monotonously reciting viewpoint — one read, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A droning speaker gives an opinion that someone has read out.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to speak in a level chanting voice, so the person doing it fits.

clue.text: Ape synod's unusual times for public visits

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of the two words are reshuffled

parts.note: the 's stands for is, joining the fodder to its signal, so only synod gives letters

explanation.surface: A church council of apes would certainly be an odd sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'synod's' as 'synod is': the 's is a link, leaving APE SYNOD to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Days when schools, colleges or institutions admit the public to look around.

clue.text: Go down for a season in San Francisco?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to drop or descend
second meaning: the American word for autumn

explanation.walkthrough: San Francisco stands for American usage, where the season is named for the leaves coming down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to drop downward and, in American English, the autumn months.
